## 1. Deeds like ashes on a stormy day  (`#ashes-on-a-stormy-day`)

Cited ayat: 14:18

> **14:18** مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِرَبِّهِمْ أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ كَرَمَادٍ ٱشْتَدَّتْ بِهِ ٱلرِّيحُ فِى يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ لَّا يَقْدِرُونَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا۟ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلضَّلَٰلُ ٱلْبَعِيدُ

### Claims

**c1** (14:18): The ayah says that the similitude of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes that the wind blows hard on a stormy day.

**c2** (14:18): They have no power over anything of what they earned.

**c3** (14:18): That, the ayah says, is the far error.

### One-minute summary

The ayah likens the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord to ashes that the wind blows hard on a stormy day [c1]. They have no power over anything of what they earned [c2].

### Complete story

The ayah says that the similitude of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes [c1]. The wind blows hard on the ashes on a stormy day [c1]. They have no power over anything of what they earned [c2]. That, the ayah says, is the far error [c3].

### Deep study

The ayah gives the similitude in one sentence and then states what follows about those it describes: they have no power over what they earned, and this is the far error [c1][c2][c3]. The picture is of ashes, which are light, and of a wind that blows hard [c1].

### Kids mode

The ayah says that the deeds of those who disbelieve in their Lord are like ashes [c1]. On a stormy day the wind blows hard on them [c1]. They have no power over anything of what they earned [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture shows deeds that cannot be gathered back once the wind has taken them [c1][c2]. Another reading is that the ayah calls this the far error [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which deeds are meant, or who in particular is meant by those who disbelieve in their Lord; no person is named.
- Not established: how the ayah relates to the other ayat on deeds that are lost; this draft cites only 14:18.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal).
- The words ashtaddat bihi al-rih (the wind blew hard on it) and al-dalal al-baid (the far error) are rendered here in plain words; a scholar may prefer other wording.
